A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GradPCA and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation; the reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original GradPCA and baseline evaluations on CIFAR and ImageNet, runtime measurements, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, near-OOD and ViT results, and original seed, layer, training-data, and label-noise studies.

M1.justification: V2 Remark 3.3 changes the stated default scalar output from summed logits to the maximum logit, revising which gradients are computed. The class-mean PCA procedure and existing variants remain. However, v2 Section 5 and Appendix C.1 still describe averaging/summing, leaving the aggregation used for the reported results unresolved.

E1.justification: The original CIFAR and ImageNet coverage remains. V2 adds CIFAR-10 versus CIFAR-100 as a distinct near-OOD scenario (Table 5) and uses MNIST for the NTK illustrations (Figure 1, Appendix E.10). MNIST is not presented as an additional OOD detection benchmark.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated comparisons with Revisited PCA, Projected Gradients, Kernel PCA (CoRP), and the basic NCI detector in Tables 1, 2, and 4. Several were discussed or cited in v1 but not evaluated there. These additions substantially strengthen comparison with methods closely related to GradPCA.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands the evaluation design with ViT-B/16 and VGG16 configurations, block/unit parameter sweeps, fitting on 10–90% of ImageNet training data, and fixed label-corruption experiments. The NTK illustrations also introduce specified sampling and training procedures. Existing main benchmark splits, AUROC/FPR95 metrics, and original threshold, sparsity, and batch-size settings remain.

E4.justification: V2 retains the original threshold, sparsity, and batch-size ablations but expands selected-layer comparisons into systematic block/unit studies. It adds near-OOD robustness, training-seed stability, training-data sensitivity, label-noise degradation, and NTK structure illustrations. Table 13 adds retained-component counts to the existing threshold results, providing a substantive memory analysis.

E5.justification: V2 adds ten independently trained VGG16 seeds with per-seed results in Table 7. It also removes displayed uncertainty from GradOrth in Tables 1–2 and removes the standard deviations for Mahalanobis, KNN, and ReAct in Table 2, although their three-run descriptions remain in Appendix C.2.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive comparator and appendix results and replaces GradOrth scores. In Table 2, GradOrth's ImageNet BiT-S average AUROC changes from 60.36 ± 1.09 to 90.34, above unchanged GradPCA at 90.22; the revisions are not explained as a same-procedure gain. Table 1 also changes dataset-specific assignments: TIMM GradPCA's Places AUROC becomes 84.63 instead of 87.31, while appendix Tables 12 and 15 retain 87.31.

T1.justification: The principal theorems, assumptions, bounds, examples, and Appendix B proofs retain their mathematical substance. Theorem 4.2 is renamed as an OOD certificate. The added eigenvector-lifting and cosine-score formulas explain existing operations rather than introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims about NTK-based gradient PCA, consistent detection, spectral theory, and feature quality. The new emphasis on one-sided per-sample certificates restates guarantees already claimed by v1's sufficient-condition theorems rather than expanding their scope.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly adds dependence on ID labels and restriction to classification tasks as limitations. It explains layer-selection results through alignment strength and motivates angular scoring. Appendix C.2 removes v1's caveat about uncertain GradOrth implementation fidelity and its explanation of poor GradOrth performance.

D1.justification: V2 adds a concrete code-repository link, implementation settings for the new baselines, and training details for the NTK illustrations. Most existing framework-conversion, hardware, and runtime information remains. Access documentation is inconsistent: the introduction provides the repository, while the new reproducibility statement still promises public release upon acceptance.

R1.justification: V2 adds references and discussion covering NCI, GROOD, other gradient-based approaches, training-seed sensitivity, and layerwise feature learning. Section 2 more explicitly acknowledges gradient-spectral predecessors already discussed in v1's appendix. The overall taxonomy and NTK-alignment novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized rewrites to the contributions, spectral motivation, results discussion, and limitations, and organizes algorithm explanations into Remarks 3.1–3.4. It adds reproducibility, acknowledgement, and LLM-use statements and adopts conference headers and author-year citations. The main section sequence and much of the original prose remain.

P2.justification: V2 adds NTK heatmaps and tables for the new benchmarks and analyses. Existing benchmark tables gain comparator rows, Table 1 gains a label-requirement column, and colored ranking highlights become bold/underlined formatting. Tables are repositioned and reformatted; the original performance chart remains as Figure 2.

improvement.justification: The closer baseline comparisons and targeted robustness studies make v2's empirical evidence more informative, while the added label and classification limitations clarify applicability. These gains are tempered by conflicting aggregation descriptions, unexplained GradOrth score revisions, removed ImageNet uncertainty reporting, and discrepancies between Table 1 and retained appendix values. The revision provides a useful net improvement, but these reporting problems limit its overall benefit.
